title: Delhi HC: Possession Under a Family Arrangement Cannot Later Be Recast as Adverse Possession
card_summary: A claimant sought ownership of a shop he had occupied for decades, but the trial court rejected his suit under Order VII Rule 11 CPC. The High Court upheld that rejection, holding long possession alone does not confer ownership where he never pleaded his possession turned hostile to the true owner's title. His own case traced the occupation to a family arrangement among cousins, not adverse possession.
card_tip: A plaint claiming adverse possession must plead the specific date and conduct that made possession hostile; occupation that began by family consent will not convert into ownership merely through the passage of time.
verification_notes: The appeal number RFA 393/2026, the 28 September 2026 decision date, Justice Neena Bansal Krishna's bench, the shop property and family-arrangement background, and the holding on adverse possession are drawn from the Delhi High Court's own judgment record (NBK28092026RFA3932026) together with Advocate Gandhi's commentary and the Caseon case record; the full reasoning in the order was not independently retrieved beyond these summaries.
